data.plain: A doctrine document gains authority only when it passes the grammar, has its required fields, lists the result records it must produce and the statements of what it does not cover (its anti-claims), and has a validator that checks it. Until it has that executable contract, its prose can help a reader find their way and has no authority over the system.

analogy.boundary: The inspection picture covers only when a notice may govern; it says nothing about whether the room is well built or the code complete.

maps.analogy: the 'meets code' notice on the door
maps.doctrine: a doctrine document the system may treat as a rule
the required fields and result-record obligations

maps.analogy: the notice saying what it does and does not certify
maps.doctrine: the stated limits of the rule

maps.analogy: a well-worded sign nobody inspected, which informs and authorizes nothing
maps.doctrine: prose that guides readers and governs nothing

analogy.text: A 'meets code' notice on a door controls who may enter only after an inspector checks the room against the building code with every required sign-off. A well-worded sign nobody inspected just informs people.

reader.counterexample: A persuasive markdown standard is used as the rule other components must meet, although nothing parses it against a grammar and it lists no records or limits.
reader.does_not_prove: Passing the grammar shows a document is well formed, and its content can still be wrong.

example.text: The executable doctrine grammar accepts a standard as a rule only when it parses under the grammar and carries its required fields, result-record obligations and stated limits, so a standard written only as prose stays a description.

reader.governs: When a doctrine document may act as a rule for other components.
reader.plain: A written rule can govern other parts of the system only after a program checks its form and finds its required parts and stated limits. Well-written words alone can guide a reader and nothing more.
reader.potential_misread: That clear, confident writing is enough to make something a binding rule, when passing the form check only means it is well formed.
reader.refuses: Giving unstructured prose the authority of a rule without the executable contract.
reader.requires: Passing the grammar, plus the required fields, result-record obligations and stated limits.
reader.why_it_matters: A persuasive paragraph cannot be treated as a rule other parts must obey before anything has checked it.
